finding: The shared pairing of western geography and a ḥ-s-n word raises a possible association: 7:137 places the earth’s east and west beside the completion of the good promise for Israel, while 18:86 brings ḥusnan into a scene at the sun’s setting place.

evidence.ar: مَغْرِبَ ٱلشَّمْسِ
تَتَّخِذَ فِيهِمْ حُسْنًۭا
مَشَٰرِقَ ٱلْأَرْضِ وَمَغَٰرِبَهَا
وَتَمَّتْ كَلِمَتُ رَبِّكَ ٱلْحُسْنَىٰ عَلَىٰ بَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ بِمَا صَبَرُوا۟

missing: A clearer Qur’anic pattern or textual cue connecting the setting-place and ḥusnan in 18:86 with the east-west inheritance and fulfilled promise in 7:137 could establish an echo; the shared root pair alone does not.

finding: 73:9 joins God’s dominion over east and west to taking Him as wakīl; 18:84–86 says God enabled Dhul-Qarnayn and places a decision at the sun’s west, which could frame his local rule as authority under divine sovereignty.

evidence.ar: رَّبُّ ٱلْمَشْرِقِ وَٱلْمَغْرِبِ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ فَٱتَّخِذْهُ وَكِيلًۭا
إِنَّا مَكَّنَّا لَهُۥ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ وَءَاتَيْنَٰهُ مِن كُلِّ شَىْءٍۢ سَبَبًۭا
مَغْرِبَ ٱلشَّمْسِ
وَإِمَّآ أَن تَتَّخِذَ فِيهِمْ حُسْنًۭا

missing: An explicit signal linking 73:9 to Dhul-Qarnayn’s authority could establish this frame. The verbs share a root, but 73:9 takes God as wakīl whereas 18:86 takes ḥusnan among the people.

finding: 48:25 withholds punitive harm where unknown believers are intermixed with disbelievers, then says the disbelievers would have been punished if the groups were separated. Beside 18:86’s choice and 18:87’s focus on whoever wrongs, it raises whether punishment is meant to track moral status rather than group identity.

evidence.ar: وَلَوْلَا رِجَالٌۭ مُّؤْمِنُونَ وَنِسَآءٌۭ مُّؤْمِنَٰتٌۭ لَّمْ تَعْلَمُوهُمْ أَن تَطَـُٔوهُمْ فَتُصِيبَكُم مِّنْهُم مَّعَرَّةٌۢ بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍۢ
لَوْ تَزَيَّلُوا۟ لَعَذَّبْنَا ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ مِنْهُمْ عَذَابًا أَلِيمًا
وَجَدَ عِندَهَا قَوْمًۭا ۗ قُلْنَا يَٰذَا ٱلْقَرْنَيْنِ إِمَّآ أَن تُعَذِّبَ وَإِمَّآ أَن تَتَّخِذَ فِيهِمْ حُسْنًۭا
أَمَّا مَن ظَلَمَ فَسَوْفَ نُعَذِّبُهُۥ

missing: The focus passage does not say its people are mixed like those in 48:25; evidence tying these communities together or a repeated formulation could establish the comparison. The next ayah supplies a moral criterion, but not the group’s composition.

finding: A possible contrast is worldly display versus ethical good: 19:74 calls earlier qarn generations superior in furnishings and spectacle, while 18:46 calls wealth and children adornment and abiding good deeds better. This may resonate with 18:86’s title al-Qarnayn beside its option of ḥusnan, if the title can evoke qarn as generation.

evidence.ar: وَكَمْ أَهْلَكْنَا قَبْلَهُم مِّن قَرْنٍ هُمْ أَحْسَنُ أَثَٰثًۭا وَرِءْيًۭا
ٱلْمَالُ وَٱلْبَنُونَ زِينَةُ ٱلْحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا ۖ وَٱلْبَٰقِيَٰتُ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتُ خَيْرٌ عِندَ رَبِّكَ ثَوَابًۭا وَخَيْرٌ أَمَلًۭا
يَٰذَا ٱلْقَرْنَيْنِ
تَتَّخِذَ فِيهِمْ حُسْنًۭا

missing: A lexical account showing that al-Qarnayn here evokes qarn meaning generation, or a clearer textual echo between these passages, could strengthen the contrast; 19:74 uses a comparative about worldly appearance while 18:86 offers goodness as conduct.

finding: 28:78 places a speaker’s claim that wealth came from knowledge “with me” beside God’s destruction of earlier generations; 18:84 and 18:95 instead describe Dhul-Qarnayn’s reach as enabled by his Lord. This could cast the choice in 18:86 as a test of how power is sourced and used.

evidence.ar: قَالَ إِنَّمَآ أُوتِيتُهُۥ عَلَىٰ عِلْمٍ عِندِىٓ ۚ أَوَلَمْ يَعْلَمْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ قَدْ أَهْلَكَ مِن قَبْلِهِۦ مِنَ ٱلْقُرُونِ مَنْ هُوَ أَشَدُّ مِنْهُ قُوَّةًۭ وَأَكْثَرُ جَمْعًۭا
إِنَّا مَكَّنَّا لَهُۥ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ وَءَاتَيْنَٰهُ مِن كُلِّ شَىْءٍۢ سَبَبًۭا
يَٰذَا ٱلْقَرْنَيْنِ
قَالَ مَا مَكَّنِّى فِيهِ رَبِّى خَيْرٌۭ

missing: No explicit connection joins the speaker of 28:78 to Dhul-Qarnayn. Here ٱلْقُرُونِ means generations, whereas ٱلْقَرْنَيْنِ is a title with an unresolved sense; a clearer narrative echo or lexical link could establish the comparison.

finding: 11:31 warns against deciding that people cannot receive God’s good on the basis of how an audience’s eyes regard them. Since 18:86 leaves its qawm undescribed and offers punishment or goodness, then 18:87–88 specify ethical grounds, this comparison could raise how a ruler should discern among people.

evidence.ar: وَلَآ أَقُولُ لِلَّذِينَ تَزْدَرِىٓ أَعْيُنُكُمْ لَن يُؤْتِيَهُمُ ٱللَّهُ خَيْرًا
وَوَجَدَ عِندَهَا قَوْمًۭا ۗ قُلْنَا يَٰذَا ٱلْقَرْنَيْنِ إِمَّآ أَن تُعَذِّبَ وَإِمَّآ أَن تَتَّخِذَ فِيهِمْ حُسْنًۭا
أَمَّا مَن ظَلَمَ فَسَوْفَ نُعَذِّبُهُۥ
وَأَمَّا مَنْ ءَامَنَ وَعَمِلَ صَٰلِحًۭا فَلَهُۥ جَزَآءً ٱلْحُسْنَىٰ

missing: 18:86 does not say its people are weak, despised, or judged by appearance, and Noah addresses another audience. A cue about the group’s standing or a repeated formulation could connect the scenes.

finding: 18:86 begins a repeated itinerary pattern: reaching an endpoint with حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا بَلَغَ, then finding the sun and people; 18:90 mirrors it at sunrise, and 18:93 carries the reaching-and-finding frame to the two barriers. The western encounter is one stage in a sequence of meetings with distinct communities.

evidence.ar: حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا بَلَغَ مَغْرِبَ ٱلشَّمْسِ وَجَدَهَا تَغْرُبُ فِى عَيْنٍ حَمِئَةٍۢ وَوَجَدَ عِندَهَا قَوْمًۭا
حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا بَلَغَ مَطْلِعَ ٱلشَّمْسِ وَجَدَهَا تَطْلُعُ عَلَىٰ قَوْمٍۢ لَّمْ نَجْعَل لَّهُم مِّن دُونِهَا سِتْرًۭا
حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا بَلَغَ بَيْنَ ٱلسَّدَّيْنِ وَجَدَ مِن دُونِهِمَا قَوْمًۭا لَّا يَكَادُونَ يَفْقَهُونَ قَوْلًۭا

activation: The west/sun-setting frame in 18:86 is repeated with the sunrise frame in 18:90, followed by the same arrival and discovery syntax in 18:93; each stage introduces a different people and response.
limits: The repeated structure establishes a narrative pattern, not that the communities are identical or face the same decision; the outcomes and descriptions differ.
